subject: Post-call: model-fit deep-dive + fncall / JSON schema next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@luminaryhealth.io>, Evan Cho <evan.cho@luminaryhealth.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model-fit deep-dive + fncall / JSON schema next steps

Hi Sofia / Evan —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum:

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goal: extract structured eligibility & benefits recommendations from clinical intake notes (free-text), produce JSON order objects that downstream systems can consume.
- Key constraints you emphasized: max 3s median generation latency, PII redaction before storage, and deterministic structured fields for downstream reconciliation.
- Current infra: Luminary runs validation in-house; wants a small eval (1k sample records) to validate model fit and fncall reliability before a broader POC.

Proposed evaluation plan (what Redwood will run / hand over)
1) Model shortlist for initial runs (we'll spin 1k-record batches):
   - rw-13b-8bit (Redwood-verified 13B quant) — good latency/cost balance for structured extraction.
   - mistral-7b-instruct-v1 — strong instruction-following for short clinical notes.
   - llama2-chat-70b-q4f32 (fallback run for hard cases) — higher quality when schema fails but higher cost.

2) Benchmarks we will produce:
   - Token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95), cost per 1k records, and schema compliance rate (exact match on required fields).
   - Regression checks: run the same prompt set vs baseline mapping to detect drop-offs in key fields (payer_code, diagnosis_code).

3) Structured output + function-calling tests:
   - JSON schema we'll validate against: your required fields + normalized enums. We'll run both strict and permissive validation.
   - For fncall flows, we'll test retry logic: 3 attempts with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms -> 1800ms) and K/V cache warm-up for multi-turn records.

4) Pass/fail criteria (for initial 1k run):
   - Schema compliance >= 94% (strict) OR >= 98% (permissive) with automated patches flagged.
   - Median latency <= 3s for the chosen Dedicated config.
   - No PII leakage in returned tool calls (we will run PII detection scans).

Action items from Redwood (deliverables):
- Run the 1k benchmark across the three candidate models, provide a per-model report (latency, cost, schema compliance), annotated failure examples, and a short remediation list (prompt tweaks, schema relaxations, quantization profile).
- Share prompt sets and the JSON schema we’ll validate against (attached draft below).
- Provide a canary rollout suggestion and fallback policy if schema compliance drops (auto-fallback to llama2-chat-70b-q4f32 for non-compliant records).

Attachments included in this thread: prompt_set_v1.csv, json_schema_order_v2.json (draft), sample records (anonymized).

Proposed next steps (please reply with confirmations):
- Sofia/Evan: share a 1k anonymized sample export (CSV) by Monday so we can queue the run.
- We'll target internal delivery of the benchmark report by Wednesday EOD PT if we have samples Monday morning.
- Kick-off call to review results: propose Thu 10am PT — would that work?

Thanks — I put Monica on copy to coordinate the sample transfer and the SOW follow-up.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@luminaryhealth.io>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit deep-dive + fncall / JSON schema next steps

Thanks Rafael — this is great and aligns with our internal ask. Quick clarifications from our side before we send the CSV: 

1) Data constraints: we'll strip direct identifiers (names, MRN) but keep demographic fields (age_range, zip3) — is that sufficient for your schema checks?
2) Latency: 3s median is a hard target for our UI. If rw-13b-8bit meets schema but slightly above latency, can we evaluate a Dedicated node with slightly higher CPU/GPU?
3) PII policy: we need proof of PII redaction checks in the report. Can Redwood include the detection output and explain redaction heuristics?

We will upload a 1k anonymized CSV to the Drive folder by Monday 11am PT. Attaching a small sample row here (inlined) so you can sanity-check the mapping: 

"patient_note","visit_date","location","preferred_language","raw_payload_id"
"Pt reports chest pain and referred to cardiology. PCP believes labs pending. Possible prior MI noted.","2027-04-28","San Jose, CA","en","row-0001"

Also flag: we have an internal enum for payer_code that must map to Redwood's normalized payer enum — we'll include the mapping doc in the upload.

We'll hold Thu 10am PT as tentative — Evan confirmed that works for him.

— Sofia

Luminary Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@luminaryhealth.io>, Evan Cho <evan.cho@luminaryhealth.io>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model-fit deep-dive + fncall / JSON schema next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks for the sample row and clarifications, that mapping note is helpful. A few commitments from our side and logistics: 

Logistics and security
- Please upload the 1k anonymized CSV to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF_benchmark-playbooks and grant redwood-inference@redwood.ai view + download. We'll only use the files for the benchmark run and delete them after the report unless you instruct otherwise.
- For PII checks: we'll run two detectors — heuristic (regex + token lists) and an ML model that flags likely PII spans. We will include the detection results as a CSV that maps row ids -> flagged spans. That file will be included in the deliverable.

Evaluation specifics (technical)
- Schema validation: we'll run both strict (exact types + enums) and tolerant (coerce strings -> enums where safe) validators and report both pass rates.
- Retry / fncall behavior: our recommended pattern for the production POC is: immediate attempt -> if validation fails, run a single automatic patch prompt (a 'schema-fixer' prompt) and retry. If still failing, escalate to a queued human-in-the-loop job. We will include the 'schema-fixer' prompt and examples in the appendix.
- Canary policy: 5% traffic canary for 24 hours, monitor schema compliance and latency; auto-fallback to a more robust model (llama2-chat-70b-q4f32) for records that hit the human queue repeatedly.

Deliverables and timeline
- Monday 11am PT: you upload the 1k CSV.
- Monday 1pm PT: Redwood starts the 1k runs (three models) on Dedicated dev pool.
- Wednesday EOD PT: Redwood delivers benchmark report + annotated failures + prompt_set_v1.csv + schema validator outputs.
- Thu 10am PT: 30-min review call (we'll share a calendar invite).

Attachments in this thread: SOW-draft-Luminary-v1.pdf (SOW draft for initial 1k eval), rw-benchmark-results-template.xlsx (template we'll fill).

If that all sounds good we'll proceed — Rafael / Karthik will monitor the runs and Marissa will handle commercial questions.

Best,
Monica Patel
Manager, Solutions Ops — Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks Sofia. I've created the Drive folder and uploaded the SOW draft and prompt set; you should see the invite in your Drive. I'll also create the run ticket and include the benchmark playbook link here: https://redwood-inference.internal/benchmarks/luminary-fit-2027-05

Calendar invite: Thu 27 May 2027 10:00 AM PT — invite sent (30 min).

Two quick technical notes we will surface in the report:
- For schema-fixer retries we recommend keeping prompt length small and targeting only the failing fields (not the entire JSON blob) to reduce hallucination risk. We'll include before/after examples in the appendix.
- We'll capture per-field confidence scores and include a threshold you can use to auto-send low-confidence records to the human queue.

If you can confirm the Drive upload and that the SOW is acceptable, Marissa will follow up on contracting/credits.

See you Thu.
